text:
ashley: quick q — re: canary + automatic fallback: how do we handle per-tenant session affinity when the canary variant keeps a different KV-cached context?

diego: do we have to guarantee sticky sessions to the same model variant for session length? that gets messy with scaling.

priya: my vote: short-lived session tokens for canaries (<= 5 min). if a request hits fallback, rehydrate prefix from central cache + accept slight mismatch.

ashley: mismatch is the scary part for chat UX. customers will see context drift. can we instead route only new sessions to canary and keep existing sessions on stable?

sam_k: that's what we did in the prototype: route by session-state flag. new session => canary 5%. existing session => pinned to original variant. but edge-case: when canary is promoted, we need bulk-migration.

priya: bulk-migration is doable async: spawn a background job to warm KV for affected sessions then switch pin. fallbacks during migration use stable + log mismatch metric.

ashley: ok. what about automatic fallback triggers? latency SLO breach, error rate, quality regression (eval signal). which are primary?

diego: order: safety first. 1) infra errors (5xx) immediate failover, 2) latency SLO (p50/p95 breach thresholds), 3) quality regression (slow-moving, needs eval window).

sam_k: implementing 2) needs a short smoothing window so transient spikes don't flip us. 30s rolling + 3 consecutive windows ~ 90s.

ashley: agreed. we should also degrade gracefully — fallback to cheaper quantized variant, not always full stable model. fallback hierarchy: canary -> quantized-variant -> stable.

priya: +1. note: quantized variant may not support some token-level APIs (tooling/callables). we need capability negotiation in the router.

ashley: good catch. router should have capability matrix per variant. fallback only to compatible variants, otherwise fallback to stable.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/tenant-slice=5% by ashley @ 3512349950

oncall-bot: probe: latency p95 380ms -> threshold 300ms (canary slice). alerting to #eng-oncall

diego: seen the probe. temporary throttle the canary slice to 1% and spin up additional canary workers? or toggle fallback aggressiveness?

sam_k: throttle to 1% now, and increase circuit sensitivity (lower thresholds) until probe stabilizes. also start warming quantized variant for that slice.

ashley: sounds good. can we codify policy as a small DSL? e.g.:
```
fallback_policy:
  - trigger: infra_5xx >= 1%
    action: immediate_fallback
  - trigger: p95_latency > 300ms for 90s
    action: reduce_slice: 1%
  - trigger: quality_drop >= 2 points over 1h
    action: rollback_candidate
  - migration: async_warm_then_flip: true
```

priya: love the DSL. router will need a safe-mode that enforces min-capacity for warmup and respects tenant isolation.

diego: we must also record deterministic audit events for every automatic fallback (reason, metric snapshot, decision path) for postmortem/eval.

ashley: logging + telemetry is required. also include the exact model hash and quantization profile used.

sam_k: final ops note — keep the human-in-the-loop override. automatic fallback ok, but must notify owners and expose a one-click promote/rollback in console. :thumbsup:

ashley: agreed. i'll update RFC with: session pinning for existing sessions, new-session slicing, fallback hierarchy (quantized -> stable), DSL for triggers, 90s smoothing, capability matrix check, audit events, and admin overrides. will post PR in the next hour.

priya: cheers. ping me if you want the warming job snippet.

diego: i can add the capability matrix to the model registry API.

ashley: thanks all. closing for now. :white_check_mark:
